title: RAG at scale: production ready GenAI apps with Azure AI Search

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is retrieval system design including hybrid search, cross-encoder reranking, quantization, and integrated ingestion for RAG at scale. The entire talk is about Azure AI Search as an enterprise search and knowledge-base system for generative AI applications. The speaker explicitly frames the shift from 2023 prototypes to 2024 production and addresses production scale challenges throughout. The content assumes familiarity with RAG applications and covers vector search internals, quantization trade-offs, and two-stage retrieval architecture. Recorded live conference talk at the AI Engineer World's Fair with Jupyter notebook demonstrations. Thirteen evidence anchors from the transcript directly support the retrieval-focused classification with specific technical claims and demonstrations.

summary: Pablo, a Distinguished Engineer at Microsoft in the Azure AI team, presents on RAG at scale with focus on the retrieval portion. He recaps three approaches for integrating domain knowledge with language models: prompt engineering (effective with longer context models), fine-tuning (for teaching patterns or domain jargon), and retrieval augmented generation (for data the model did not see during training). RAG separates reasoning from knowledge, using an orchestration component to query a knowledge base and pass candidates to the language model. The shift from 2023 prototypes to 2024 production introduces scale pressures: data volume growth, increased rate of change, higher query loads, more complex multi-step workflows, and more diverse data types. Azure AI Search is positioned as a complete retrieval system combining vector database capabilities with Microsoft's broader retrieval experience and Azure enterprise readiness, supporting HNSW approximate nearest neighbor search, exhaustive search, filtering, column projection, multi-vector queries, and hybrid search fusing vector and keyword results. Pablo demonstrates index creation and search operations in a Jupyter notebook. He emphasizes quality as the most important production consideration and introduces Azure AI Search's two-stage retrieval system: the first stage is recall-oriented, using vectors, keywords, and recall-oriented tricks to produce many candidates; the second stage reranks candidates using a cross-encoder transformer model that sees both the document and query simultaneously, producing higher-quality rankings than cosine similarity alone. Reranking adds approximately 100 milliseconds of latency, largely hidden behind the LLM call. Hybrid search with fusion plus reranking consistently outperforms keyword-only (BM25), vector-only, or fusion-only approaches. Pablo also discusses significantly increased vector density limits (10-12x on the same SKUs), enabling multi-billion vector applications. OpenAI uses Azure AI Search to back ChatGPT file and Assistants API vector stores, increasing user limits 500x. Quantization options include int8 and single-bit encoding, the latter achieving 32x vector density with low-to-mid 90% original performance, with remaining precision recoverable through reranking. Azure AI Search supports all these types with optional automatic quantization and oversampling using stored full-precision data. Finally, an integrated ingestion system handles automated connection to Azure data sources (Blob Storage, OneLake, Cosmos DB), change tracking, file format processing (PDFs, Office documents, images, nested formats), chunking, vectorization, and indexing in a continuously running industrial-strength pipeline.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and RAG Recap
sections.summary: Pablo introduces himself as a Microsoft Distinguished Engineer in the Azure AI team. He recaps three options for domain knowledge with LLMs: prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and RAG. RAG separates reasoning (LLM) from knowledge (external base) via an orchestration component that queries the knowledge base and passes candidates to the model. He notes the audience is already working on RAG applications.

sections.title: Scale Challenges in Production RAG
sections.summary: Pablo describes the shift from 2023 prototypes to 2024 production, introducing scale pressures: data volume growth, increased rate of change, higher query loads, more complex multi-step workflows, and more diverse data types and sources. He positions Azure AI Search as an integrated retrieval system combining vector search with Microsoft's broader retrieval experience and Azure enterprise readiness.

sections.title: Azure AI Search Vector Capabilities
sections.summary: Pablo outlines Azure AI Search's vector search features: fast approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW), exhaustive search for baselines, filtering, column projection, and multi-vector support for documents with different content parts or data types using different embeddings.

sections.title: Demo: Index Creation and Search
sections.summary: Pablo demonstrates creating an Azure AI Search index from scratch in a Jupyter notebook with categorical, text, and vector fields (dimension 3, HNSW). He indexes data, performs vector search, hybrid text-plus-vector search with fusion, and filtered search by category. He explains that hybrid search returns more results than K nearest neighbors because candidates come from both vector and keyword paths before fusion.

sections.title: Quality and Two-Stage Retrieval
sections.summary: Pablo emphasizes quality as the most important production consideration: application success depends on whether the retrieval system found the right information. He introduces Azure AI Search's two-stage retrieval system, recall-oriented in the first stage, as the approach used by sophisticated search engines.

sections.title: Two-Stage Retrieval and Cross-Encoder Reranking
sections.summary: Pablo explains the second stage reranks candidates using a cross-encoder transformer model that sees both document and query simultaneously, producing higher quality than cosine similarity. Reranking adds approximately 100 milliseconds, largely hidden behind the LLM call. He shows that hybrid search with fusion plus reranking outperforms keyword-only (BM25), vector-only, and fusion-only approaches. He notes that scoping the dataset using discrete metadata is the most effective quality improvement before applying ranking techniques.

sections.title: Vector Density Limits and Scale
sections.summary: Pablo announces significantly increased vector density limits (10-12x on same SKUs, no price change), enabling multi-billion vector applications. He notes OpenAI uses Azure AI Search to back ChatGPT file and Assistants API vector stores, increasing user limits 500x. He references a slide with detailed new limits for the audience.

sections.title: Quantization Options
sections.summary: Pablo covers quantization options: int8 and single-bit encoding. Single-bit quantization achieves 32x vector density with low-to-mid 90% original performance; Cohere independently observed approximately 95% precision retention with binary encoding. Remaining precision is recoverable through reranking. Azure AI Search supports all quantization types with optional automatic quantization and oversampling using stored full-precision data for reranking, giving users control over the quality-density-speed trade-off.

sections.title: Integrated Ingestion Pipeline and Conclusion
sections.summary: Pablo describes Azure AI Search's integrated ingestion system with integrated vectorization: automatic connection to Azure data sources (Blob Storage, OneLake, Cosmos DB), security handling, change tracking with incremental processing cost, multi-format file processing (PDFs, Office documents, images, nested formats), chunking, vectorization, and indexing in a continuously running pipeline. He encourages the audience to try Azure AI Search, noting subscriptions include a free instance.
